bocRate.context: Overnight rate at 2.25%, the seventh consecutive hold at this level. Prime rate 6.09%.

realGdp.context: Monthly real GDP contracted 0.6%. Manufacturing -1.4% M/M and -4.6% YoY; management of companies (NAICS 55) -4.1% M/M and -21.9% YoY. Construction +1.1% M/M offsets a portion.

cpi.context: Headline CPI at +1.8% YoY in March 2026. Provincial dispersion: PE +5.4% high, ON -1.1% low. Within BoC 1-3% target band.

unemployment.context: National unemployment 6.7%. Provincial range SK 5.0% (lowest) to NL 9.5% (highest), a 4.5pp spread.

housingStarts.context: Housing starts at 250,900 SAAR. Single/multi splits last refreshed 2025-12-01.

tradeBalance.context: Trade deficit widened to $3.6B from $1.3B. Exports fell 4.7% to $62.5B; imports declined 1.1% to $66.1B. Motor vehicle exports dropped 21.2%.

retailSales.context: Retail sales rose 1.1% to $70.7B. Core retail (ex gasoline and motor vehicles) up 0.9%. Motor vehicle dealers led gains (+2.0%). Advance estimate for February: +0.9%.

consumerConfidence.context: Consumer confidence declined to 47.50 from 49.30 in January. Bloomberg/Nanos index showed a three-week slide into late March.

participation.context: Participation rate 64.9%. Period is 71 days old at refresh date — older than the 45-day freshness threshold.

employmentChange.context: Employment declined 84,000 in February after gaining 76,000 in January. Full-time employment fell 108,000.

cross_references.interpretation: Manufacturing GDP contraction registers in monthly and annual prints; pipeline tracks 52 manufacturing projects ($67.4B).
Construction sector GDP advances despite the broader monthly decline; pipeline tracks 1687 infrastructure projects ($179.0B).
Mining and oil and gas GDP rises 1.2% M/M against a flat year-ago base; pipeline tracks 367 mining projects and 61 oil and gas projects.
NAICS 55 records the deepest annual contraction among 20 tracked industries at -21.9% YoY.
Housing starts steady at 250,900 SAAR; pipeline tracks 211 residential projects ($44.4B). Capex intentions for 2026 are $401.2B with $274.0B in construction.
